Everything in the Hardening group is available to switch on.
Soft, Block and most guards work without this. Kiosk, Safe Mode blocking, app suspension and uninstall protection do not.
Safe Mode can be closed
Otherwise a reboot into Safe Mode starts the phone with FocusLock switched off.
Blocked apps can be suspended
The system refuses to launch them, instead of FocusLock catching them a moment late.
Blocked apps can be hidden
They disappear from the launcher for the length of a session.
FocusLock can be the home screen
During a kiosk session the home button lands here instead of the launcher.
Uninstalling can be blocked
Removing the app stops being a way to end a session early.
Browsers can be held to your allowlist
Chrome and friends get a managed policy pointing at the same list the safe browser uses.
Every one of these is still a switch in Rules. Being Device Owner makes them possible, not automatic.
Sign out of every Google account on this phone, and remove any other user or work profile. Android refuses to set a Device Owner while an account exists.
On the phone: Settings, About phone, tap Build number seven times to unlock Developer options.
In Developer options, turn on USB debugging.
Plug the phone into a computer with the Android platform-tools installed, and accept the debugging prompt on the phone.
On the computer, run: adb devices, and check the phone is listed as device rather than unauthorized.
Run the command below.
Come back here. This screen should now say Active.

On a phone that has been factory reset, tapping the welcome screen six times opens a QR scanner. Provisioning from a QR sets Device Owner without a computer, but it needs the app hosted at a URL along with its signature checksum, and it wipes the phone as part of setup. The ADB route above is the practical one for a phone already in use.
A factory reset always works
Recovery-mode reset is the ultimate exit and no software tier can close it. FocusLock does not try, and never removes the reset button from the You tab.
ADB stays yours to close
Provisioning does not disable ADB. Only the button in the You tab does, and only when you tap it.
Nothing is remote
There is no server, no account and no one else who can lock or unlock this phone.
adb shell am broadcast -a com.focuslock.mdm.ADB_COMMAND --es cmd stop_session --ez confirm true
Advanced, explained
What each mode sets, what you can change, and how to get out.
The four modes
Ending a session
Breaks
If you are locked in and need out
A mode is a starting point
Picking a mode loads a set of switches. It does not lock those switches. Every one of them is in You → Advanced, and whatever you set there is what runs.
Your changes stick. The template is only re-loaded when you pick a different mode, which is the one moment you have clearly asked for it.
Kiosk is the only mode that pins the phone to FocusLock and closes the launcher. It needs Device Owner.
\"End a session early\" is a switch in You → Advanced, not a property of the mode.
On
An \"End this session\" button appears on the Focus tab. Everything unlocks straight away, and the time you already did still counts.
Off
No button. The session runs until its timer ends.
Kiosk

Loads with it off, because that is what choosing Kiosk means. You can turn it back on — the switch is not hidden from you — but be honest with yourself about whether you are turning it on now or turning it on later at 1am.
Turning it off does not survive being forgotten: the timer still ends on its own.
A break unlocks one blocked app for a few minutes, then re-locks it by itself.
Why it exists
The alternative is abandoning the whole session for one thing you needed. A bounded exception keeps the rest of the session alive.
Taking one is not a failure
It is a feature you switched on deliberately. Nothing counts it against you, and no streak breaks.
Your numbers
Length and how many a day are yours to set, in You → Advanced or on the Daily limits screen.
In order, least destructive first.
1. Wait
Every session has a timer. When it ends, everything unlocks on its own. This is the intended exit and costs you nothing.
2. Turn the early exit back on
You → Advanced → \"End a session early\". Works in every mode, including Kiosk.
3. From a computer
If the phone is pinned and you cannot reach Advanced, one ADB command ends the session. It refuses to run without the confirm flag, so it cannot happen by accident.
4. Factory reset
The last resort, and the only one that always works. It releases Device Owner and wipes the phone. FocusLock never blocks it — the button is on the You tab, behind a countdown.
